q: How do you evaluate a RAG system?
a: Separately for retrieval (recall@k, precision@k, MRR, NDCG against gold passages) and generation (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision and recall, correctness vs reference), on a curated golden set run on every change, plus human review and production feedback. RAGAS or a calibrated LLM judge automates scoring; LangSmith traces each step.
The share of claims in the answer that are supported by the retrieved context. 3 of 4 claims supported → 0.75. It measures groundedness, not correctness.

q: High faithfulness but users say answers are wrong. How?
a: The answer faithfully reflects the wrong or outdated context. Check context recall and correctness against references; look at retrieval (stale documents, missing filters on date/version) and document governance.

Improve retrieval first; instruct to answer only from context and say "I don't know"; require citations; abstain on low retrieval scores; low temperature; put the best chunks first; run a groundedness check before returning; and evaluate continuously.
LLMs tend to use information at the start and end of a long context better than information in the middle. Keep the context short and place the most relevant chunks first (or last).

q: How do you make LLM-as-judge reliable?
a: Clear rubric, give it the question, context, answer and reference, ask for reasoning then a score, prefer pairwise comparisons, randomise order to avoid position bias, check agreement with human labels on a sample, and use a different or stronger model than the one being judged.

q: How do you build a golden evaluation set?
a: 50–300 questions from real users or experts with reference answers and source passages, covering easy, hard, multi-hop, table, out-of-scope and adversarial cases. Bootstrap with LLM-generated questions from the documents and have experts review. Version it and run it in CI.

q: Compute MRR: first relevant hit at ranks 1, 3, and not found.
Why separate retrieval from generation evaluation?
a: A wrong answer can come from a missed chunk or from the LLM misusing a good chunk. Measuring recall@k and faithfulness separately tells you which component to fix.

q: For retrieval, recall or precision: which matters more?
a: Recall, at the first stage: a missing chunk can't be recovered, while an extra irrelevant one can be filtered by the reranker or ignored. Precision matters for the final few chunks in the prompt.

q: How do you evaluate without many labelled questions?
a: Generate questions per chunk with an LLM (the source chunk becomes the gold label), have experts review a sample, add real user questions as they arrive, and freeze and version the set.
